title: Brian Schottenheimer on 105.3 The Fan | 9-24-26
headline: Cowboys travel to Rio to face Baltimore in Week 3; Schottenheimer raves about Donovan Ezeiruaku and Caleb Downs, says CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens can each go off, and hints at managing snap counts for the D-line and skill players. No injuries were mentioned.
summary: Schottenheimer said the Cowboys treated this as a short week, giving players Monday off and finishing the full game plan before flying to Rio to face the Ravens. The team has planned the trip since March, with sleep and travel experts consulted, and will practice Friday and visit the stadium Saturday. He said the field is expected to be fine and that the team has cleats available and has been educating players, with Rashan Gary having played in a similar game. On defense, the focus is building a wall at the line against Derrick Henry and containing Lamar Jackson, which Dallas has not done well in the first two weeks. He called for a big game from the front and from the safeties, not only linebackers Dee Winters and Jaishawn Barham. He praised Quinnen Williams and Kenny Clark as elite competitors, but said the staff is looking at rotations and play counts early in the season, which also applies to Pickens, Lamb and the tight ends. He said Caleb Downs is ahead of where he was in Week 1, wants him involved early, and cited his pass breakup on Terry McLaurin. He said Lamb has practiced crisply and that Lamb or Pickens could be the featured player in any given week. He called Donovan Ezeiruaku's play awesome, with a growing pass-rush toolbox, and expects Trey Hendrickson to line up on the left against Tyler Guyton.

signals.claim: Lamb will remain a featured receiver, and the leading target can alternate between him and George Pickens from week to week.
signals.note: Lamb is practicing sharply and the target share can swing between him and Pickens, so weekly volume is somewhat volatile but the ceiling is high.
signals.quote: if it's CD one week, it could be George the next week

signals.claim: Pickens shares the top receiving role with Lamb and could be the lead target in any given week.
signals.note: Both receivers are WR1-caliber and either can have a huge game, as the two combined for big yardage recently.

signals.claim: Downs will be involved early in games with plays called to get him going, and he is improving week over week.
signals.note: Strong IDP trajectory for Downs, though his impact may not always show up in box-score stats.
signals.quote: he's a guy also that you want to get involved early.

signals.claim: Ezeiruaku continues to develop as a pass rusher and sacks are expected to come.
signals.note: He is generating pressure and the coach is optimistic that sacks will come, which helps IDP value.
signals.quote: he's playing awesome. He really is.

signals.claim: Clark's snaps may be managed through rotations, with the staff considering taking some load off.
signals.note: Possible snap reduction for the interior D-line could cap IDP production.
signals.quote: do we need to take a little bit something off them?

signals.claim: Williams is facing questions about his play, and the staff is reviewing his technique and play count.
signals.note: Coach defended him as an elite competitor but acknowledged the team has not played its best.

signals.claim: Winters will be asked to fill gaps against Derrick Henry, but the coach stressed safeties and the front share the responsibility.
signals.note: Run-stopping linebacker role against Baltimore could mean tackle volume, though the coach spread the responsibility.
signals.quote: it's not just going to be D and J. Sean filling gaps.

signals.claim: Barham will be asked to fill gaps against Derrick Henry alongside Winters.
signals.note: Likely high-tackle-opportunity matchup vs. the Ravens' run game.

signals.claim: Guyton will face Trey Hendrickson, who plays mainly on the left side.
signals.note: A tough pass-rush matchup for Guyton could affect pass protection and Dak Prescott's pressure rate.
signals.quote: it should be a great matchup between him and Tyler Guyton.

topics.detail: The team moved its week forward, gave players Monday off, and completed the game plan before flying to Rio. They will practice Friday and tour the stadium Saturday, and the coach said the field should be fine.

Dallas aims to create a wall at the line to stop Derrick Henry and has made containing Lamar Jackson and plastering coverage on extended plays a major emphasis, admitting the team has struggled with it.
The staff is monitoring play counts and rest periods for linemen, receivers like Pickens and Lamb, and tight ends, comparing it to star basketball players getting rest.

title: Nick Sirianni Press Conference: September 24, 2026
headline: Zach Ertz signed as tight end help with Dallas Goedert apparently on IR, but his Sunday readiness is unknown. Saquon Barkley's status hangs on the injury report after he left the last game, and Tank Bigsby and Will Shipley are trusted backups.
summary: Sirianni previewed the Bears, saying Chicago's quarterback uncertainty adds layers to the prep but is routine in the NFL. He praised the Bears' coaching and their run game, including a Bears running back he coached last year, and stressed block destruction and fundamentals. He said the team works in pads every Wednesday for that reason. Zach Ertz is newly signed and had not practiced yet, so his knowledge of the system and readiness for Sunday are still to be determined, and Sirianni said he would quiz him and watch him in practice. A reporter's question implied Dallas Goedert is on IR, and Sirianni did not dispute it. He did not give specifics on Saquon Barkley beyond pointing to the injury report, but he referred to Saquon being unable to continue in the last game. He said the backups, Tank Bigsby and Will Shipley, were majorly helpful in that game, have different skill sets, and have both earned reps. Newly signed DB Kenny Moore drew heavy praise for his competitiveness and versatility, though Sirianni did not commit to him playing safety and said he needs reps. Sirianni also praised Dontayvion Wicks for his physicality, competitiveness and contested-catch ability, and explained that the team has no takeaway yet because of a lack of opportunities rather than poor process.

injuries.detail: Sirianni referred to him being unable to continue in the last game and said the injury report will show his status. A reporter noted he was practicing a bit, and Sirianni gave no timeline or concern level.
A reporter's question framed him as on IR with an injury history, and Sirianni did not dispute it. This is why Ertz was added.
Newly signed and had not yet practiced. Sirianni said he would see where Ertz is after the practice.

signals.claim: Ertz's role and whether he plays Sunday will be decided after he practices this week.
signals.note: With Goedert apparently on IR, Ertz is a potential TE option, but his Week 3 usage depends on how quickly he learns the offense.
signals.quote: see where he is and see how we need to play this thing out

signals.claim: Barkley's availability for the Bears game will be shown on the injury report.
signals.note: He left the last game, so his practice participation this week is the key signal for his fantasy availability.
signals.quote: We'll get you guys injury report.

signals.claim: Bigsby will share backup running back work behind Barkley and see more reps if Barkley is limited.
signals.note: He is a handcuff-type pickup if Barkley's injury lingers.
signals.quote: We trust the heck out of both of them.

signals.claim: Shipley will share backup running back work with Bigsby and see more if Barkley is limited.
signals.note: He is part of a committee behind Barkley, which makes the backup split murky.
signals.quote: they both have earned reps and they both, you know, have different things

signals.note: Sirianni sees him as a valuable addition and a contested-catch weapon, which supports his place in the receiver rotation.
signals.quote: I love his physicality within the game of football and his mentality

signals.claim: Moore may be used in a versatile role, possibly at safety, once he gets reps in practice.
signals.note: This is mainly relevant for IDP leagues, and his role is not yet defined.
signals.quote: he has ability to to be versatile, which is really important

topics.detail: The Bears' unsettled quarterback situation adds more layers to the game plan, but Sirianni called it routine and said the team will follow its usual process.

topics.topic: Bears run game and run defense
topics.detail: Sirianni called the Bears' run game challenging and praised their RB's one-cut ability. He said block destruction by the O-line and D-line will be critical, and the team practices in pads every Wednesday to improve it.
He said takeaways come in bunches, the team has not dropped an interception, and scrambling QBs have limited strip-sack chances. He will not sacrifice tackling fundamentals to chase strips.
Sirianni said the team does not get into revenge for last year's loss to the Bears, and the keys are turnovers, explosive plays and fundamentals.
He said a head coach should not worry about pleasing outsiders and should be authentic within the rules.

title: WATCH: Mike McCarthy Media Availability (Sept. 24)
headline: McCarthy backs DK Metcalf ("we're going to throw the ball to DK") and is all for more Pat Freiermuth targets; the injury status of "Joey" stays vague and the offense is still working combinations.
summary: McCarthy praised Asante Samuel Jr., who has been consistent since day one and has put together two solid outings, but he faces a big challenge this week. He was evasive about a player the reporter called "Joey", saying only that the player hit his planned work on Wednesday and has more scheduled Thursday, and he pointed reporters to the injury report. On personnel, he said the team will keep working different combinations all week, mainly on offense, while the game plan goes in. Against the Bengals he expects four-, five- and six-man line looks, including a six-one look in the red zone, and the Steelers are preparing for anything. He said his long history with Aaron Rodgers makes the planning conversations longer, and that the offense is built around his experience and fits the perimeter players. McCarthy endorsed getting Pat Freiermuth more targets, saying he has earned them and that the team needs more ball distribution overall. He backed DK Metcalf through his bumps, promising he will get targets and opportunities Sunday. He also praised Patrick Graham's defense for fitting schemes to players' skills, and noted the corners must grow on special teams, naming Daylen Everette as a good practice performer.

injuries.detail: McCarthy said he hit his planned work Wednesday, with more scheduled Thursday. He would not say whether the player was limited and pointed to the injury report.

signals.claim: DK Metcalf will keep getting targets and will have opportunities in Sunday's game against the Bengals.
signals.note: Metcalf has had a slow start, but the coach is publicly committed to feeding him, which supports a bounce-back.
signals.quote: We're going to throw the ball to DK. You know I can promise you that.

signals.claim: The Steelers want to get Pat Freiermuth more targets and a more balanced target distribution.
signals.note: Rodgers and McCarthy both want Freiermuth more involved, which is a TE upside signal, though McCarthy hedged on game flow.
signals.quote: Pat's playing really well. He's earned those opportunities.

signals.claim: Asante Samuel Jr. will face a big challenge this week against the Bengals' receivers.
signals.note: He has played well, but the matchup is tough, which matters for opposing Bengals WRs in fantasy.

signals.claim: Daylen Everette should keep growing on special teams and be ready to play at corner.
signals.note: He is depth with a chance at a bigger role, a minor IDP and defensive-depth note.
signals.quote: I think Everett's one of them. So I actually had a nice day here yesterday

signals.claim: The offense will keep being tailored to Rodgers' experience, with longer conversations and the first 15 scripted plays set Thursday night.
signals.note: The scheme is still being tailored to Rodgers, so passing game continuity is still developing.
signals.quote: it's about playing to his reps and to his experiences.

topics.detail: Cincinnati has stopped the run well without loading the box. They show four-, five- and six-man line fronts, including a six-one look in the red zone. Pittsburgh is working on all of them and playing the numbers.
The Steelers will keep working different combinations through the week while installing the game plan. No specific changes were named.
McCarthy praised Graham's staff for building schemes around players' individual skills, including pass rush plans and in-game adjustments. Communication has been good.
Wednesday was the best Wednesday of the season. McCarthy views the first four weeks of the season as a continuation of training camp and wants the team to keep growing.
